floor_basis_legend: controlling=SCOTUS on omitted question; controlling-anchor=cluster origin; controlling-fold-candidate=controlling but may fold as a bullet under an existing/anchor page; both-legs-controlling=both blind legs independently proposed; split-resolver=SCOTUS resolved a named circuit split; binding-in-circuit=circuit-court on omitted question; mention=below floor

caption: Marcus v. Search Warrant
note: ORIGIN of the special-seizure-rules-for-expressive-material line: mass seizure of allegedly obscene publications under warrants leaving selection to officers lacked required safeguards (unbridled-discretion). Corpus has the PROGENY (A Quantity of Copies of Books v. Kansas) + Stanford/Lo-Ji/Macon but not the parent. grep 0. Cross-proposed by foundations-codex; filed here. See DW2-1.

caption: Roaden v. Kentucky
note: Warrantless seizure of a film after a sheriff viewed it was unreasonable; expressive-material seizures require PRIOR JUDICIAL APPROVAL absent true now-or-never exigency -> suppression. Distinct suppression-side anchor of the cluster; not payload-carried by the issuance cases in corpus. grep 0. See DW2-1.

caption: Lee Art Theatre, Inc. v. Virginia
note: A warrant on a police officer's conclusory obscenity assertion, without the magistrate probing the factual basis, was constitutionally insufficient; seized films inadmissible. Refines the affidavit-sufficiency prong. Fold-candidate under the expressive-material block. See DW2-1.

caption: Heller v. New York
verified: knowledge+grep(absent all sources); distinct from District of Columbia v. Heller (in manifest)
note: A single evidentiary copy may be seized under an ex parte warrant after a neutral magistrate's probable-obscenity determination if a prompt adversary hearing + copying/return safeguards protect continued exhibition. Refines the execution/remedy prong. Fold-candidate. See DW2-1.

caption: New York v. P. J. Video, Inc.
note: First Amendment imposes NO higher probable-cause standard for warrants targeting presumptively protected material; Gates fair-probability governs. Refines the PC-standard prong. Fold-candidate. See DW2-1.

caption: Fort Wayne Books, Inc. v. Indiana
note: Mere probable cause cannot support pretrial seizure of an entire bookstore's expressive inventory (RICO); final obscenity adjudication required first. Seizure-scope prong (RICO-forfeiture overlap w/ w1 forfeiture set). Fold-candidate. See DW2-1.

caption: South Dakota v. Neville
note: FIELD-facing + admissibility: admitting a suspect's REFUSAL to take a BAC test does not violate the 5A privilege, and DP did not require a warning that refusal is usable. Distinct 5A question not carried by Schmerber/Muniz/Birchfield (4A). Squarely in remit (chemical-test request + suppression of refusal evidence). claude confessions leg asserted saturation and missed it (leg-diff).

caption: Kansas v. Ventris
note: MASSIAH remedy/admissibility (REMIT GUARD: Massiah/suppression-facing STAYS): a statement elicited by a jailhouse informant in 6A violation is excluded from the case-in-chief but admissible to IMPEACH. claude RTC leg listed the Massiah line complete but omitted the impeachment-exception (leg-diff).

caption: Weatherford v. Bursey
note: ANCHOR of the government-intrusion-into-attorney-client-relationship doctrine (a distinct 6A sub-node the corpus lacks entirely): an undercover agent's presence at defense meetings is NOT a per se 6A violation where he did not seek/transmit defense strategy; rejects automatic liability/new-trial. In remit (undercover-agent investigative conduct + officer civil-liability boundary). Morrison/Black/O'Brien fold under it as mentions.

caption: Moore v. Illinois
verified: knowledge+grep(only a cross-ref bullet inside cases/Kirby v. Illinois.md; no standalone page; distinct from Virginia v. Moore in manifest)
note: BOTH BLIND LEGS. A corporeal one-on-one identification at a POST-CHARGE preliminary hearing without counsel = 6A critical stage (Wade/Gilbert), and the uncounseled pretrial ID cannot buttress the case-in-chief even on independent source (Gilbert per se rule). Identification-facing/suppression-side = squarely in remit; fills the placed-empty 'Lineups and the Right to Counsel' stub. Filed once here (cross-home: fair-trial/Eyewitness ID) to avoid double-count.

caption: California v. Trombetta
note: BOTH BLIND LEGS. Anchor prong 1 of the due-process DUTY-TO-PRESERVE evidence line (the officer-side mirror of Brady's duty to DISCLOSE, entirely absent from corpus): constitutional duty limited to evidence with exculpatory value APPARENT BEFORE destruction and not otherwise reasonably obtainable. Suppression-side / officer evidence-handling = in remit.

caption: Arizona v. Youngblood
note: BOTH BLIND LEGS. THE anchor of the duty-to-preserve trilogy: for merely POTENTIALLY USEFUL evidence, defendant must show police BAD FAITH; negligence/good-faith mistake is not a DP violation. Frames every police-lost-evidence / spoliation suppression motion. In remit.

caption: Illinois v. Fisher
verified: knowledge+grep(absent all sources); distinct from Michigan v. Fisher (in manifest)
note: BOTH BLIND LEGS. Completes the trilogy: the Youngblood bad-faith requirement applies to potentially-useful evidence REGARDLESS of a pending discovery request. BORDERLINE page-vs-fold under a Youngblood-anchored page (D5) -- see DW2-6.

caption: Rochin v. California
note: FIELD-conduct + DP-suppression: evidence obtained by conscience-shocking police conduct (forcible stomach-pumping) cannot be used consistent with DP -- the substantive-DP 'shocks the conscience' + bodily-intrusion ancestor Schmerber expressly distinguishes. Borderline history-vs-page (payload partly carried by County of Sacramento v. Lewis + absorbed into Mapp) -- see DW2-7.

caption: Briscoe v. LaHue
note: OFFICER CIVIL-LIABILITY boundary (§1983 witness-immunity tier -- see Part-2 DW2-8): police officers have ABSOLUTE witness immunity from §1983 damages for alleged perjury as trial witnesses. Immunity-at-trial prong NAMED, but it is officer-liability doctrine (the corpus §1983 node's wheelhouse), not defendant trial-craft. In remit.

caption: Rehberg v. Paulk
note: Extends Briscoe: GRAND-JURY witnesses -- including a government INVESTIGATOR -- get the same absolute §1983 immunity as trial witnesses. Officer-liability (§1983 absolute-immunity structure). Pairs with Briscoe (anchor) + is the officer-investigator application; may fold as a Briscoe bullet.

caption: McDonough v. Smith
note: SPLIT-RESOLVER (clears the split-marker prong): a §1983 FABRICATED-EVIDENCE claim accrues at favorable termination of the criminal proceeding -- resolving the 2d Cir. earlier-accrual rule against the 5th/6th/9th favorable-termination approach. §1983 officer-liability accrual (pairs w/ in-corpus Heck v. Humphrey + w1 Wallace v. Kato).

caption: Ex parte Jackson
note: FOUNDATIONAL protected-papers/sealed-mail case: sealed letters/packages in the mail are protected 'papers' openable only under a 4A warrant (oath/particularity). Baseline the corpus mail-line (Van Leeuwen detention / Ramsey border mail) builds on but never states. Borderline history-vs-page -- see DW2-7. claude foundations leg asserted saturation (leg-diff).

caption: Kastigar v. United States
note: DISPOSITION SPLIT (DW2-2). Use-and-derivative-use immunity coextensive w/ 5A; gov't bears independent-source burden. Home is grand-jury/immunity-grant (immunity-at-trial) -> REMIT GUARD floor; Garrity fruits/wall payload already in corpus via Garrity + Lefkowitz v. Turley. Related-case row on the Garrity page.

caption: Uniformed Sanitation Men Assn., Inc. v. Commissioner of Sanitation
note: DW2-4. Same-day companion to Gardner v. Broderick (IN CORPUS); public employees can't be forced to choose job vs 5A immunity. Payload = Gardner's -> subsumed; below floor.

caption: New Jersey v. Portash
note: DW2-4. Immunized grand-jury testimony can't be used even to impeach -> immunity-at-trial impeachment-use (contrast to in-corpus Harris v. New York). REMIT GUARD floor; Related-case row on Garrity page.

caption: Harrison v. United States
note: DW2-3. Prior trial testimony impelled by gov't's illegal use of confessions is inadmissible at retrial (gov't burden). Narrow confession-fruits-at-retrial application subsumed by in-corpus Wong Sun fruits doctrine; trial-testimony-as-fruit is trial-adjacent.

caption: United States v. Morrison
note: DW2-3. Remedy companion to Weatherford: post-charge gov't-agent contact w/ represented defendant -> no dismissal absent prejudice; tailored remedy. Remedy-craft; operative intrusion/remedy rule carried by the Weatherford page.

caption: United States v. Valenzuela-Bernal
note: DW2-4. Deportation of alien witnesses violates DP/compulsory process only on a plausible materiality+favorability showing. Compulsory-process/witness-materiality = trial-side standard -> REMIT GUARD floor.

caption: Killian v. United States
note: DW2-3. Good-faith destruction of preliminary FBI notes required no relief once final reports produced -- narrow evidence-preservation PRECURSOR subsumed by the Trombetta/Youngblood/Fisher trilogy now paged.

caption: United States v. Ackerman
note: DW2-5. WEB-VERIFIED (Gorsuch; NCMEC = governmental agent; opening unopened email = 4A search exceeding Jacobsen/Walter via Jones trespass). Single-circuit; the hash-match private-search-SCOPE split it feeds is ALREADY corpus-flagged (Fourth Amendment Framework: Wilson 9th / Reddick 5th / Miller 6th, both in manifest); NCMEC-state-action alone has no clean both-sides split -> below floor.

caption: Reid v. Georgia
note: DW2-3. Per-curiam RS-floor: a thin drug-courier profile matching many innocent travelers did not establish reasonable suspicion. Subsumed by the exhaustively-complete PC/RS page (Sokolow/Arvizu totality). Related-case marker.

caption: United States v. Di Re
note: DW2-3. Foundational PC-floor: mere presence/association can't supply PC; fruits can't retroactively justify. Operative rule carried by in-corpus Ybarra v. Illinois + Maryland v. Pringle. Related-case marker.

caption: Hunter v. Bryant
note: DW2-3. QI protects officers who reasonably-but-mistakenly find PC ('arguable probable cause'). Subsumed by the in-corpus QI line (Malley v. Briggs / District of Columbia v. Wesby / al-Kidd). Related-case marker.

caption: Lefkowitz v. Cunningham
note: Penalty-case extension of Garrity/Turley (party-office stripped to compel non-immunized testimony). Codex filed as mention; below floor. Distinct from in-corpus Lefkowitz v. Turley.

caption: Michigan v. Harvey
note: Impeachment use of a statement taken in violation of the now-OVERRULED Michigan v. Jackson prophylactic rule; historical -- Ventris is the cleaner current Massiah-impeachment authority.

caption: Black v. United States
note: Per-curiam attorney-client eavesdropping remand; fact-bound; background to Weatherford/Morrison. Distinct from in-manifest united-states-v-black (10th Cir.).

caption: O'Brien v. United States
note: Terse per-curiam post-indictment eavesdropping remand following Black; subsumed by Weatherford/Morrison intrusion/remedy rule.

caption: Coleman v. Alabama
note: Preliminary hearing is a critical stage requiring counsel -- but trial-PROCESS craft (counsel's cross/discovery function), not field/ID conduct; attachment payload carried by in-corpus Rothgery. REMIT GUARD EXCLUDE-leaning. Distinct from Coleman v. Thompson.

caption: Marron v. United States
note: Foundational particularity ('nothing left to the discretion of the officer executing the warrant'); operationally carried by in-corpus Stanford/Groh/Steele (and cited within cases/Stanford v. Texas.md). History/PRACTICES fold, not a page.

caption: In re Winship
note: Proof BEYOND A REASONABLE DOUBT is the constitutional conviction standard -- the TOP rung of the Proof Ladder, expressly a trial/conviction (non-field) standard. Out of field remit; Related-case row if the Proof Ladder stub is authored.

caption: Addington v. Texas
note: CLEAR AND CONVINCING evidence -- the intermediate CIVIL rung (e.g., civil commitment). Out of field remit; Related-case row completing the Proof Ladder above probable cause.

caption: Youngblood bad-faith definition open + state-constitutional departures
note: Below the split-marker floor: 'bad faith' left undefined (diffuse circuit divergence, not a clean both-sides split) + many state high courts reject the bad-faith requirement under their own constitutions. Recent-developments note if a Youngblood page is authored; no pending SCOTUS case.

caption: Imbler v. Pachtman
note: PART-2 §1983 STRUCTURAL FIND. ANCHOR of ABSOLUTE prosecutorial immunity: a prosecutor has ABSOLUTE §1983 immunity for acts intimately associated with the judicial phase (initiating a prosecution, presenting the State's case). The corpus §1983 node pages QUALIFIED immunity (Malley/al-Kidd/Harlow/Pearson) and MUNICIPAL liability (Monell/Canton/Pembaur/Brown/Connick) but has ZERO of the absolute-immunity tier. grep 0 everywhere. Strong page-candidate.

caption: Buckley v. Fitzsimmons
note: PART-2 §1983 STRUCTURAL FIND. The FUNCTIONAL LIMIT of Imbler and the officer-relevant one: NO absolute immunity for INVESTIGATIVE acts (fabricating evidence during the pre-charge investigation) or press statements -- those get only QUALIFIED immunity. Draws the advocacy-vs-investigation line that governs when a prosecutor/officer-adjacent actor is exposed. grep 0 everywhere. Pairs w/ Imbler.

caption: United States v. New York Telephone Co.
note: PART-2 TITLE III FIND (borderline). Title III does NOT govern PEN REGISTERS (they don't 'intercept' communication 'contents') -- the statutory-SCOPE holding that produced the separate Pen Register Act and set up Smith v. Maryland; AND the All Writs Act empowers a court to compel provider assistance (doctrinal ancestor of the compelled-technical-assistance debate). 4A pen-register payload carried by in-corpus Smith v. Maryland, but the statutory-scope + All-Writs holdings are distinct and grep 0. Borderline page-vs-mention; the ONLY residual Title III omission after w1 added Keith/Giordano/Donovan/Scott + Warshak.

caption: Kalina v. Fletcher
note: PART-2 §1983 refinement (below floor): a prosecutor who personally vouches for facts in a warrant affidavit acts as a COMPLAINING WITNESS -> only QUALIFIED immunity. Refines the Imbler/Buckley advocacy-vs-investigation line; Related-case bullet under an Imbler/Buckley page.

caption: Kentucky v. Graham
note: PART-2 §1983 refinement (below floor): official-capacity vs personal-capacity suits + §1988 fee exposure -- refines in-corpus Will v. Michigan Dept. of State Police (w1) + Hafer v. Melo (w1). Related-case bullet.
